weeks.title: The Anatomy of a Compelling Story

assignments.title: Practical 1 — The Power of Words
assignments.description:
Theme: Expand your vocabulary. Elevate your communication.

A good communicator does not just know what to say. They know how to express their thoughts clearly, accurately and effectively.

The words you use influence how people understand your ideas and how effectively you communicate.

For this practical, you will be working with ten vocabulary words over seven days, then recording a short video explaining all ten in your own words.
assignments.instructions:
YOUR TEN WORDS

1. ARTICULATE
Meaning: To express thoughts, ideas or feelings clearly and effectively.
Example: "She was able to articulate her concerns without creating unnecessary tension."

2. DELIBERATE
Meaning: Done consciously, carefully and with intention.
Example: "I am making a deliberate effort to improve my communication skills."

3. PRAGMATIC
Meaning: Practical and focused on what works in a real situation.
Example: "We need a pragmatic solution to this problem."

4. NUANCED
Meaning: Showing subtle differences, details or complexities that are not immediately obvious.
Example: "That is a nuanced argument, and I think we should examine both sides."

5. COMPELLING
Meaning: Extremely interesting, convincing or persuasive.
Example: "She presented a compelling argument that changed our perspective."

6. RESILIENT
Meaning: Able to recover, adapt or remain strong when facing difficulties.
Example: "A resilient person learns to adapt when circumstances become difficult."

7. METICULOUS
Meaning: Extremely careful and attentive to details.
Example: "He was meticulous when preparing the presentation."

8. AMBIGUOUS
Meaning: Unclear or capable of having more than one interpretation.
Example: "Your instructions are ambiguous. Could you explain what you mean?"

9. ALLEVIATE
Meaning: To reduce or make something less severe, painful or difficult.
Example: "A little preparation can alleviate the anxiety that comes with public speaking."

10. FACILITATE
Meaning: To make a process or activity easier or help it happen.
Example: "Good communication facilitates effective teamwork."

YOUR TASK

You are required to master these ten words and incorporate them naturally into your everyday communication.

For the next seven days:

1. Learn the meaning of each word.
2. Understand how and when to use it.
3. Practise pronouncing each word correctly.
4. Use at least one of the ten words in your everyday conversations each day.
5. You may use two or three words in the same conversation where appropriate.
6. Do not force a word into a sentence where it does not belong.

Use the words in actual conversations, messages, discussions, meetings and presentations.

YOUR DAILY CHALLENGE

At the end of each day, write down:

- The word or words you used.
- The sentence or conversation in which you used them.
- Whether you used them correctly.
- What you learned about using them.

FINAL TASK

At the end of the seven days, record a short video of yourself explaining all ten words in your own words and using each in an original sentence.

Do not simply read the definitions provided here. Demonstrate that you understand them.

THE OBJECTIVE

We want you to move beyond memorising vocabulary. We want you to develop the ability to express yourself with greater precision, confidence and clarity.

Remember: a bigger vocabulary is only useful when you know how to use it.
assignments.requirements:
WHAT YOU WILL BE GRADED ON

1. COMPLETION — Did you record a video covering all ten words?

2. OWN WORDS — Did you explain each word yourself rather than reading the definitions given?

3. ORIGINAL SENTENCES — Is each word used in a sentence you wrote, not the example supplied?

4. CORRECT USAGE — Is each word used accurately and in the right context?

5. PRONUNCIATION — Are the words pronounced correctly and clearly?

6. DAILY RECORD — Did you keep the seven-day log of words used, with the sentence and what you learned?

7. DELIVERY — Is the video clear, audible and reasonably presented?

assignments.title: Practical 2 — Your First TED-Style Talk
assignments.description:
Theme: Think clearly. Speak confidently. Influence meaningfully.

Imagine you have been invited to speak at a TEDx event.

You are standing on a stage. There is an audience in front of you. Everyone is waiting to hear what you have to say.

You have one opportunity to communicate an idea that makes people think differently.

This is your challenge.

YOUR TOPIC

"The Danger of Living a Life You Never Questioned."

How many of the decisions we make are actually ours? The careers we pursue, the lifestyles we desire, the expectations we accept, the things we consider success and even the way we measure our progress.

How much of what we believe comes from our own thinking, and how much have we simply inherited from our environment?

Your task is to explore this idea and communicate your perspective.
assignments.instructions:
YOUR TASK

Record a TED-style presentation lasting 3-5 minutes on the topic.

However, there is one important condition:

YOU MUST NOT USE A SCRIPT.

No reading from your phone. No reading from a notebook. No memorised paragraphs.

You are expected to think through the topic, organise your ideas and deliver your presentation naturally.

You may prepare by researching the subject, reflecting on personal experiences and arranging your main points mentally.

But when recording, speak directly to the camera without reading a prepared script.

WHAT YOUR PRESENTATION SHOULD CONTAIN

1. A STRONG OPENING

Start with something that captures attention. It could be:

- A thought-provoking question.
- A surprising observation.
- A personal experience.
- A statement that challenges a common belief.

Avoid beginning with "Good day, everyone. My name is..." Get straight into your idea.

2. YOUR CENTRAL ARGUMENT

What exactly are you trying to communicate? Establish your position clearly. Do you believe people are living according to expectations they have never questioned? Why?

3. SUPPORTING IDEAS

Develop your argument using examples, observations, experiences or relevant evidence. Don't just make statements. Explain why you believe them.

4. A MEMORABLE CONCLUSION

End with a thought, question or statement that leaves your audience thinking. Do not simply repeat your introduction.

PRESENTATION REQUIREMENTS

- Duration: 3-5 minutes.
- Format: Video presentation.
- No script or reading.
- Speak naturally and confidently.
- Maintain eye contact with the camera.
- Pay attention to your pace, clarity, tone and articulation.
- Avoid unnecessary filler words such as "erm", "like", "you know" and "basically".
- Use pauses where necessary.
- Ensure your audio is clear.

You do not need professional equipment or a fancy background. Your phone is enough.

THE OBJECTIVE

This is not an acting competition, and we are not looking for perfect presenters.

We want to see your ability to think independently, organise your thoughts and communicate an idea without depending on a written script.

You may make mistakes. You may pause. You may need to record more than once. That is part of the process.

SUBMISSION

Upload your final video presentation to Google Drive, then upload the link to the intranet. Make sure anyone with the link can access it.

Step onto the stage. Own your ideas. Make us think.
assignments.requirements:
WHAT WE ARE ASSESSING

1. CLARITY — Can you communicate your ideas in a way people understand?

2. ORGANISATION — Are your thoughts logically arranged?

3. CONFIDENCE — Do you appear comfortable expressing your ideas?

4. ARTICULATION — Are your words clear and appropriately expressed?

5. ENGAGEMENT — Can you hold the attention of your audience?

6. PERSUASIVENESS — Can you support your position and influence how people think?

7. DELIVERY — Do you use your voice, pace and pauses effectively?

8. NO SCRIPT — Did you deliver without reading from a phone, notebook or memorised paragraphs?

Note on the no-script condition: this is assessed separately because it is the point of the exercise. A fluent reading of a written script does not meet the brief, however polished it sounds.
